text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's car dealers sold 41,323 cars in January, showing 41.6 percent growth compared with the same period last year.
- Poland-based Drukpress printing house, controlled by Germany's Passauer Neue Presse group, will stop printing the Echo Krakowa daily due to overdue payments by the publisher, Drukpress said.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is considering buying a 10 percent stake in Bank Wschodnio-Europejski (BWE), Rzeczpospolita reported, quoting unofficial sources.
BWE president Ryszard Pidek did not comment on the information.
- The Lodz-based Browary Lodzkie brewery is planning to start public trading in up to three years time, when the plant's modernisation is completed, the firm's president Franciszek Tomczyk said.
- Kwidzyn municipality will not return 4.5 million zlotys to the International Paper paper mill, which IP claims overpaid taxes in 1995 and 1996.
Kwidzyn's deputy mayor Piotr Wilk said IP management has misinterpreted the taxation regulations,
- Trade exchange between Poland and Estonia was 89 million marks in 1996, well below the countries' economic potential.
Poland is Estonia's seventeenth highest trade partner, the Estonian embassy's commercial office in Warsaw said.
- Over 2.4 million firms were operating in Poland last year, which showed 14.2 percent growth compared with the year before, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The Warsaw-based PZL Warszawa aviation equipment maker's sales reached 50 million zlotys last year and net profit was at two million zlotys, the plant said.
The company is planning to start a new plant in Mexico next year.
- Warsaw-based Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) has introduced its new PBK Silver international business credit card, bearing a credit limit of 25,000 zlotys, the bank said.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Katowice and Suwalki special economic zones do not meet unemployment rate, average pay and geographic uniformity conditions set out by World Trade Organisation (WTO) regulations.
Accordingly, the zones are liable to international arbitration.
- Fiat automaker's market share in January this year was 29.4 percent, a 9.6 percent decline compared with the same period last year, a recent report by the Samar monitoring agency said.
- The Swidnik-based Zaklad Narzedziowy Swidnik tool maker has received an Interantional Standards Organisation (ISO) quality certificate, awarded by Britain's Bureau Veritas Quality International.
- Ernst & Young will soon start an open studies centre to conduct human resources management and other staff training, Ernst & Young Poland president Jerzy Cieslik said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Swarzedz furniture maker is planning to increase revenues by 68 percent this year and exports by 100 percent, the company said.
- Post Scriptum publishing, subsidised from government funds, will start publishing a new weekly next Thursday.
Poland's government was criticised for pumping taxpayer's money into the venture by independent media.
ZYCIE

- The U.S. Boeing aircraft maker has offered to participate in the production of the Polish-made Huzar military helicopter and to reinvest the profits in the country's aviation industry, Boeing North American executive George Palmer said.
PARKIET
- The listed ComputerLand software maker and systems' integrator is planning its 1997 sales to reach 255 million zlotys and to make a net profit of 15.2 million zlotys, the company forecast said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
